title: Binaliw landfill collapse kills 36 in Cebu City
summary: A large section of the privately run Binaliw sanitary landfill collapsed past 4 p.m. on 8 January 2026, burying workers and structures; 36 people died and 18 were injured. MGB-7 traced the primary cause to oversaturation of the waste mass after weeks of rain, with waste piled about 35 metres high on steep slopes. DENR-7 issued a cease-and-desist order against operator Prime Integrated Waste Solutions, forcing Cebu City to haul its garbage 61 km to Aloguinsan. On 19-20 August 2026 the DENR lifted the order with conditions, including a cap of 500 metric tons of residual waste per day, CCTV, a buffer zone and continued slope stabilisation.

timeline.actor: Prime Integrated Waste Solutions / Cebu City
timeline.note: A large portion of the Binaliw landfill collapsed past 4 p.m., burying workers and structures.
Joint inspection found oversaturation of the waste from continuous rainfall as the likely primary cause.
Cease-and-desist order issued against the operator, halting all landfill operations except rescue and cleanup.
Closure order fully lifted with conditions: 500-metric-ton daily cap, CCTV, buffer zone and a multipartite monitoring team.

title: Trash slide at Rodriguez landfill leaves one dead, two missing
summary: On the afternoon of 20 February 2026 about 420,000 cubic metres of waste eroded from the active tipping area of the Green Leap / ISWIMS sanitary landfill in Sitio Lukutan Munti, Barangay San Isidro, Rodriguez, burying three units of heavy equipment. One body was recovered and two people remained missing. DENR-EMB CALABARZON issued a cease-and-desist order on 24 February halting all operations in the six-hectare Phase 5 except retrieval, slope stabilisation and other remedial work, after inspectors found operational lapses and multiple breaches of the facility's Environmental Compliance Certificate.

timeline.actor: Green Leap Solid Waste Management / Rodriguez LGU
timeline.note: A trash slide hit Phase 5 of the landfill during compaction operations, burying three heavy-equipment units.
One body recovered, two still missing; DENR led the investigation while only Phase 5 stayed closed.
Cease-and-desist order issued against Green Leap Solid Waste Management, Inc., restricting Phase 5 to emergency and remedial activities.

title: Davao City landfill trash slide forces permanent closure
summary: A section of the garbage mound at the Davao City Sanitary Landfill in Barangay New Carmen collapsed on 20 May 2026 after heavy rains, killing two people, injuring two and leaving one missing; 123 homeowners and their dependents were evacuated. DENR-Davao suspended the landfill from 22 May, noting it received about 786 tons of waste a day and had been served a notice of violation on 19 March for operating without a discharge permit. After the city dumped uncollected garbage outside the DENR-XI office on 6 June, EMB condemned the act as unlawful. On 17 June DENR-11 ordered the permanent closure of the old landfill and a Safe Closure and Rehabilitation Plan within 30 days, and an interim cell at the adjacent new landfill was declared ready on 18 June.

timeline.note: A garbage mound collapsed at the New Carmen landfill, killing two, injuring two and leaving one missing.
Suspension of landfill use took effect so the city could implement stabilisation measures under RA 9003 and its ECC.

Final permanent closure order signed; the city must submit a Safe Closure and Rehabilitation Plan within 30 days.
Interim cell at the new sanitary landfill deemed structurally ready to receive waste.

title: Cebu City ordered to stop open dumping at South Road Properties
summary: After the Binaliw landfill closure, Cebu City used Pond A of the South Road Properties as a temporary garbage transfer station even though DENR-EMB had rejected the request on 15 January 2026. EMB-7 inspectors found the site had become an open dumpsite with mixed waste and no permit, ECC or containment, and issued a notice of violation and cease-and-desist order on 7 June. The city, which generates about 700 tons of garbage a day, was given 60 to 90 days to clear the site and haul waste to the permitted Aloguinsan facility at about P6,000 per ton. SRP transfer operations ended on 26 July 2026 as collection shifted to barangay staging areas with night-time hauling by a private contractor.

timeline.note: EMB rejected Cebu City's request to use SRP Pond A as a temporary waste transfer station.
Notice of violation under RA 9003 and a cease-and-desist order issued against the city for dumping without a permit.
City told to clear the accumulated waste within 60 to 90 days and adopt a no-touch-ground policy.
SRP transfer station closed; household trash now staged at barangays and hauled 61 km nightly to Aloguinsan.

title: Dumpsite on Aeta ancestral land in Subic shut down
summary: The Subic municipal government began dumping garbage in 2019-2020 on land inside the ancestral domain of the Ayta Ambala community in Barangay Naugsol, a move the tribe agreed to as a temporary measure during the pandemic. DENR found the site operating in violation of RA 9003 in 2022 and formally ordered its closure in November 2025, but mountains of garbage remained. On or about 15 July 2026 DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna issued a cease-and-desist order against the operator after complaints from environmental and indigenous peoples' groups. The Subic LGU says it is gradually rehabilitating the site under a plan submitted to DENR, guards have been posted to stop further dumping, and a facility in Floridablanca, Pampanga is being considered as an alternative disposal site.

timeline.note: Cease-and-desist order issued against the operator of the dump in Barangay Naugsol.
LGU says the former dumpsite is being cleaned up under a rehabilitation plan submitted to DENR, with guards posted to prevent dumping.

title: Suspected US e-waste containers flagged at Subic Bay Freeport
summary: Following alerts from the Basel Action Network and BAN Toxics about containers of suspected electronic waste shipped from the United States to the Subic Bay Freeport Zone, DENR-EMB, the Bureau of Customs and SBMA jointly inspected nine recycling locators on 1 July 2026 and convened an interagency meeting on 6 July. On 22 July the Bureau of Customs held three containers declared as scrap copper, which were tracked moving on the following day. On 5 September BAN issued a new Operation Can Opener alert identifying 184 more containers from the US expected to arrive by 30 September, urging authorities to intercept, inspect and detain them.

timeline.note: Joint inspection of nine recycling locators in the Subic Bay Freeport Zone over suspected e-waste operations.

title: Indonesian haze pushes Metro Manila air to acutely unhealthy
summary: On the morning of 1 September 2026 smoke from wildfires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, carried by the southwest monsoon, drove PM2.5 readings at 11 DENR-EMB stations in Metro Manila into the Acutely Unhealthy range, led by Parañaque at 296, Quezon City at 241, Las Piñas at 237 and Manila at 231. Navotas and Pateros registered Very Unhealthy and Makati was Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups. The EMB advised residents to limit prolonged outdoor activity and wear masks, and said conditions should gradually improve around 4-6 September if rain persists.

timeline.note: Eleven Metro Manila stations recorded Acutely Unhealthy PM2.5 levels attributed to haze from Kalimantan fires.
Advisory issued to limit outdoor activity and wear masks, with improvement expected 4-6 September if rain continues.

title: 287,442 sacks of waste pulled from Metro Manila waterways
summary: DENR-National Capital Region reported recovering 287,442 sacks of solid waste from Metro Manila's rivers, esteros and easements between January and June 2026, of which 228,396 sacks came from regular operations and 59,046 from emergency response. The Pasig River system accounted for 129,588 sacks, or about 45 percent of the total, with the Pasig River proper yielding 86,121 sacks, the San Juan River 43,467 and Estero de Paco 14,751. About 93 percent of the waste was taken directly from waterways and consisted mostly of non-biodegradable materials and floating water hyacinth.

timeline.note: First-half cleanup operations closed with 287,442 sacks of waste recovered across Metro Manila waterways.
Agency released the January-June figures and called for segregation and reduced waste generation to sustain the gains.

title: Bacolod landfill cited for leachate discharge and unpermitted cells
summary: Following a July 2026 inspection, EMB-Negros Island Region issued a notice of violation dated 10 August 2026 against the Bacolod City government over its sanitary landfill in Barangay Felisa, citing the Philippine Clean Water Act (RA 9275) for water discharged from the landfill and PD 1586 for operating Cells 4 and 5 without an Environmental Compliance Certificate. The city says Cell 4 has operated since August 2024, before the leachate pond was finished in December 2024, and that its ECC application remains pending at EMB. City Administrator Mark Steven Mayo questioned why the notice named only the LGU and not contractor IPM Construction and Development Corporation, which the city says was responsible for securing the ECC.

timeline.note: Notice of violation issued to Bacolod City for Clean Water Act breaches and operating Cells 4 and 5 without an ECC.
City reiterated compliance with landfill requirements and asked EMB to clarify why the contractor was not also cited.

sources.title: Bacolod LGU Reiterates Compliance with SLF, Seeks Clarification on EMB's Selective Issuance of Notices of Violation

title: Used syringes and medical waste dumped on Bogo City roadside
summary: Barangay personnel conducting a road-clearing activity on 11 April 2026 found used medical waste, including syringes and white plastic apparatus believed to be linked to contraceptive implants or similar procedures, dumped along an interior roadside in Barangay Cogon, Bogo City. The City Health Office and City ENRO were notified and the waste was cleared the same day on the CHO's advice. No suspects were identified because the area's CCTV cameras were still down after the magnitude 6.9 earthquake the previous year; improper disposal of hazardous waste under RA 6969 carries fines of P10,000 to P50,000.
